📌 Tehran, IRNA — Iran’s Canoeing Federation has announced that it has six representatives in the officials and referees’ section of the canoe sprint and slalom competitions at the 20th Asian Games Aichi–Nagoya 2026.

Iranian referees have taken part in officiating various editions of the Asian Games, and in the 20th Asian Games Aichi–Nagoya 2026, the country has six representatives in canoe sprint and canoe slalom.
​
In this edition, Alireza Sohrabian, Seyyed Morteza Tavakoli, Katayoun Ashraf, Atefeh Barzegar, Sasan Shojaei, and Azam Rahimizadeh will take part as Iran’s refereeing representatives in the events.
​
The competitions of the 20th Asian Games Aichi–Nagoya 2026 are scheduled to run from 19 to 27 September across venues in Aichi Prefecture in central Japan.

The DPRK has warned of the possibility of using nuclear weapons in accordance with the provisions of the law on the policy regarding the state nuclear armed forces in response to the actions of the United States and the Republic of Korea. This is stated in a statement by a representative of the DPRK Ministry of Defense, released by the Korean Central News Agency (KCNA).

The law, adopted in 2022, provides for the possibility of using nuclear weapons in the event of an attack on the country’s leadership and the nuclear force control system, as well as in the event of a threat to use nuclear or other weapons of mass destruction against the DPRK. It also allows for the use of nuclear forces in the event of a threat to strike important strategic targets and provides for the automatic delivery of a nuclear strike according to a pre‑approved plan if the nuclear force control system is under threat as a result of an attack.

 “Such threats from enemies, related to an attack and the use of weapons of mass destruction against our state, can be considered the most important challenge to ensuring security, which requires the implementation of the relevant articles of the law on the policy regarding state nuclear armed forces,” a representative of the DPRK Ministry of Defense said in a statement.

He advised the United States and the Republic of Korea to “analyze what the enforcement of the relevant articles entails and to take it as a serious warning.”

The statement was prompted by a meeting of the US–Republic of Korea Commission on Response to Weapons of Mass Destruction, which took place on September 10. According to Pyongyang, the parties agreed to improve information exchange, enhance joint response capabilities, and intensify relevant exercises.

The DPRK’s defense ministry interpreted this as preparation for the possible use of nuclear, chemical, and biological weapons against the republic. The statement also notes that similar scenarios were practiced during the joint military exercises of the United States and the Republic of Korea, Freedom Shield.

🔊 Salalah meeting unavoidable for regional security

📌 Iran and the Persian Gulf Cooperation Council (PGCC) planned to meet in Salalah, Oman, to negotiate the security of the Persian Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.

As this pen has already made clear, despite their different political viewpoints, the Arab countries of the Persian Gulf share a common view on maintaining the security of this strategic region. Iran, having the longest coastline in the Persian Gulf, also seeks enduring security in the region. A few days ago, the Spokesman of Iran's Foreign Ministry bluntly reaffirmed the importance of stability in the Persian Gulf. This proves again that despite the different political viewpoints of the countries in the region, including Iran, they have something in common: the stability and peace of the Persian Gulf, because their lives and interests are at stake.
​
The Salalah Meeting is important because:
​
First, in the short term, it can de-escalate the existing crisis, which, for political, economic, and security reasons, has dangerous dimensions for all of them. So again, scaling down this crisis is quite critical, on which they certainly have no disputes. To serve that goal, holding the meeting is very important and unavoidable. Thus, doing this is quite important—the sooner, the better—for this is a good and new opportunity they have to seize.
​
Second, in the long term, to establish lasting stability and security not only in the Persian Gulf but also in the Red Sea, they need to work out a solution. The recent crisis in the Persian Gulf proved that developments in those two regions are not only separable but also interact and reinforce each other. So the countries of these two regions have to provide a strategic mechanism and devise security arrangements.
​
Third, as I have reaffirmed before, the recent developments in the Persian Gulf, the Strait of Hormuz, as well as in the Red Sea and the Strait of Bab-el-Mandeb, have clearly proved that foreign powers cannot bring security to these two regions. Because it is the countries of these two regions who understand and are aware of all the political, economic, cultural, and security requirements of their homelands.
​
So despite their high capacities and their long stays in these areas, foreign powers do not have this possibility. By and large, these powers need to accept that their involvement in this sensitive area not only brings any security but could also erupt into uncontrollable chaos in the whole Middle East. Of course, this does not mean that those powers must not have any relations with the countries in the region. Rather, they need to behave within the framework of international law and the standards of relations with all countries of the world, provided, however, that they entrust the security of these regions to their rightful owners.
